Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

so-so phrase

also fairly well, in fair shape, so so, middling, things are going fairly well

classical

Traupman 15, 18

Variē.

Other words

  • Mediocriter quidem valeō. — fairly well

    also used · modern · Traupman 18: fairly well, mediocriter quidem valeō

    Lewis & Short has mediocriter “moderately, tolerably” as classical (corpus mediocriter aegrum, Cic. Tusc. 3.22), but not with valeō; the phrase is Traupman’s.

  • Agitur satis. — given for “things are going fairly well”

    avoid · classical · Traupman 99, 322: things are going fairly well, agitur satis; Cic. Att. 4.15.9: pugnātur ācriter: agitur tamen satis (Lewis & Short s.v. satis)

    Classically satis agere is to have one’s hands full, to be hard pressed, and Lewis & Short reads Cicero’s agitur tamen satis so: “still, it is a hard struggle” (see trouble). For “fairly well”, Variē or Mediocriter (above).

Examples

  • In mediocrī statū.

    In fair shape.Traupman 18

  • ita tenuiter

    so so (tolerably well)Traupman 382

See also not bad, as usual, average.
